title: Sum of prime divisors of neighbours
W: Add the sum of the distinct prime factors of n to that of n + 1. Tested starts reach 33 or loops through 10, 17, 30 or 107. Prove there is nothing else.

title: Lopsided neighbour map
W: Map n to P(n) + 2P(n+1). Except for the fixed point 8, every tested start falls into 23 → 29 → 39. Prove this for all starts.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+2P(n+1)$, prove every orbit not starting at $8$ reaches $(23,29,39)$.

title: The shift-6 prime map
W: Map n to P(n) + P(n+6). Tested starts reach 6 or the loop 8 ↔ 9. Prove all do.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+6)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge3$ reaches $\{6\}$ or $(8,9)$.

title: Density of the basin of 22 ↔ 34
W: For n ↦ P(n) + p(n+1), about 6% of tested starts reach the 22 ↔ 34 loop. Show the fraction has a limit and it is positive.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+p(n+1)$, prove $\lim_{x}\frac1x\#\{n\le x:\text{orbit reaches }(22,34)\}$ exists and is positive.

title: Growth rate of square-sum Hamiltonian cycles
W: Find the exponential growth rate of the number of ways to arrange 1 to N in a circle with neighbours summing to squares.
M: Determine $\lim_N\frac{\log H(N)}{N\log N}$ where $H(N)$ counts Hamiltonian cycles of $S_N$, and prove the limit exists.

title: Prime-sum Hamiltonian cycle count
W: Count the ways to arrange 1 to 2n in a circle with neighbours summing to primes. Find the growth.
M: Prove $\log C(2n)\sim 2n\log n$ (or determine the correct leading term), where $C(2n)$ counts Hamiltonian cycles of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$.

title: Square-sum matchings count
W: Count the ways to pair up 1 to N into pairs summing to squares. Find the exponential growth.
M: Determine $\lim_N\frac{\log m(N)}{N}$ (or the right normalisation) for the number $m(N)$ of perfect matchings of $S_N$, $N$ even.

title: Primes on circles centred at the origin
W: Find the largest number of prime points (p, q) lying on a single circle centred at the origin with radius up to R.
M: Determine the order of $\max_{n\le R^2}\#\{(p,q)\in\mathbb{P}^2:p^2+q^2=n\}$.

title: Thue–Morse of P(n) and P(n+1)
W: Show the Thue–Morse values at P(n) and P(n+1) are uncorrelated.

title: Two large factors and one small
W: Add P(n), P(n+1) and the smallest prime factor of n + 2. Tested starts reach 14, 33, or loops through 10, 42, 67, 97 or 3307. Prove these seven are the only fates.

title: The P(n)+P(n+2)+1 map
W: Map n to P(n) + P(n+2) + 1. Tested starts reach 6, 8, or loops through 9 (12 steps), 19 or 37. Prove these are all.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+2)+1$, prove every orbit reaches $\{6\},\{8\}$, the 12-cycle through $9$, $(19,27,33)$ or $(37,51,71,145)$.

title: Peak height of the 2n+3 map
W: For n ↦ P(2n+3) + P(n), show the highest point an orbit reaches is at most a fixed power of its start.
M: Prove there is $A$ with $\max_k f^{k}(n)\le n^{A}$ for all $n\ge3$, $f(n)=P(2n+3)+P(n)$.

title: Largest-factor subtraction game
W: From pile n you may remove P(n) stones or any prime smaller than P(n). Characterise the losing positions.
M: For moves $n\to n-q$, $q\in\mathbb{P}$, $q\le P(n)$, prove the P-positions have density zero and determine whether they are infinite.

title: Undecidability of Prime Nim variants
W: Show there is no algorithm that takes a polynomial f and decides whether the subtraction game with moves {f(p) : p prime} has eventually periodic Grundy values.
M: Prove $\{f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]:\text{Grundy sequence of the game with move set }f(\mathbb{P})\cap\mathbb{N}\text{ is eventually periodic}\}$ is undecidable, or decidable.

title: Spanning cube-sum paths
W: Show the numbers 1 to N can be lined up so neighbours sum to perfect cubes, for infinitely many N.
M: Prove the cube-sum graph $C_N$ has a Hamiltonian path for infinitely many $N$.

title: Sum-Euclid sequence
W: Start with 2 and repeatedly append the largest prime factor of one plus the sum of all previous terms. Decide whether every prime eventually appears.
M: Let $r_1=2$, $r_{n+1}=P(1+r_1+\cdots+r_n)$. Decide whether $\{r_n\}$ contains every prime.

title: Random square-sum transpositions mixing
W: Shuffle 1 to N by swapping a random pair that sums to a square. Find the mixing time and show cutoff.
M: For the random walk on $S_N$ (symmetric group) driven by uniform $T$-transpositions, $T$ as above, prove cutoff and determine its location.

title: Prime matrices generate SL2(Z)
W: Show every integer 2 by 2 matrix of determinant 1 is a product of boundedly many matrices of determinant 1 whose entries are all prime.
M: Prove there is $k$ such that every $\gamma\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ is a product of at most $k$ elements of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})\cap\mathbb{P}^{2\times2}$.

title: Largest prime factor of Markov numbers
W: Show the largest prime factor of Markov numbers tends to infinity.
M: Prove $P(m)\to\infty$ as $m$ runs through Markov numbers.

title: Apollonian packing with prime curvatures
W: In the integral Apollonian packing with curvatures (−1, 2, 2, 3), show every large prime is the largest prime factor of some circle's curvature.
M: For the $(-1,2,2,3)$ Apollonian packing with curvature multiset $\mathcal{K}$, prove $\{P(k):k\in\mathcal{K}\}$ contains all sufficiently large primes.

title: No-three-in-line in the prime grid
W: Find the largest set of prime-pair points in an N by N box with no three on a line.
M: Determine the order of $\max\{|A|:A\subseteq(\mathbb{P}\cap[1,N])^2,\text{ no three collinear}\}$.

title: Consecutive largest factors both 3 mod 4
W: Show P(n) and P(n+1) are both 3 mod 4 for a quarter of all n.
M: Prove $\#\{n\le x:P(n)\equiv P(n+1)\equiv3\ (4)\}\sim x/4$.
